title: Danya VS Magnus: Promote With the Right Piece
summary: Use checking pawn pushes and a bishop intermezzo, then choose a knight or queen according to the king’s escape.

nodes.question: Can the new white queen stop Black’s checking pawn attack?
nodes.explanation: The queen on h8 is boxed out by its own knight and pawns. Black can keep checking until the king’s route determines the right promotion.

branches.title: Source finish: bishop intermezzo and knight mate
commentary: Begin after White promotes on h8. All four remaining white pawns are retained: those on e3, e4, f4 and g2 still matter to queen access.
a2+ uses the pawn to check Kb1. White has two legal king replies, Ka1 and Kc1; the source chooses the corner.
Ka1 follows the source. The new queen cannot block an adjacent pawn check.
b2+ opens the bishop’s diagonal and offers the a2 pawn. White now has only Kxa2.
Kxa2 removes the a-pawn, but Black must improve the bishop before promoting the remaining pawn.
Bb3+ is the source intermezzo. The bishop is protected by Kc3 and checks Ka2, forcing a choice between a3 and b1.
Ka3 chooses the outward route. A queen promotion would not check this king, so Black uses a different piece.
b1=N# checks a3 with the promoted knight. Kc3 controls b2/b3/b4 and Bb3 controls a2/a4; White cannot capture the knight or block its check.
branches.explanation: b1=N# checks a3 with the promoted knight. Kc3 controls b2/b3/b4 and Bb3 controls a2/a4; White cannot capture the knight or block its check.

branches.title: Source comparison: the king returns to b1
commentary: Compare the other legal king reply to the bishop intermezzo. The earlier promotion and pawn checks stay the same.
a2+ begins the forcing pawn attack.
Ka1 enters the corner, as in the source’s main line.
b2+ checks and vacates b3 for the bishop.
Kxa2 is forced. Immediate promotion is not the source plan; the bishop first improves with tempo.
Bb3+ offers the protected bishop and checks the king.
Kb1 chooses to return toward the promotion square. Black must use the bishop to drive the king off b1.
Bc2+ checks b1 and is protected by Kc3. The white king cannot capture the bishop.
Ka2 is the sole legal move. The b2 pawn controls a1 and c1, while Black’s king controls b2.
b1=Q+ promotes with check against Ka2. Here the queen is the right piece because it keeps the attack forcing.
Ka3 is forced, with the king and bishop denying the other flights.
Qb3# finishes beside the protected black king. White’s distant queen and knight cannot answer the adjacent queen check.
branches.explanation: Qb3# finishes beside the protected black king. White’s distant queen and knight cannot answer the adjacent queen check.

branches.title: Independent defense: decline the corner
commentary: Account for the legal Kc1 reply omitted from the narrated corner line. This continuation is independently supplied.
a2+ checks Kb1. The king can choose a1 or c1; neither escapes the verified later attack.
Kc1 declines the corner, but steps onto the square attacked by a pawn arriving on b2.
b2# checks c1. The move also vacates b3, opening Ba4’s diagonal to d1; Kc3 covers b2/c2/d2, and the a2 pawn controls b1. White has no legal answer.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: b2# checks c1. The move also vacates b3, opening Ba4’s diagonal to d1; Kc3 covers b2/c2/d2, and the a2 pawn controls b1. White has no legal answer.

exercises.answer: It forces the white king to choose a3 or b1 and prepares a checking promotion appropriate to that route.

exercises.prompt: Why does one line promote to a knight and the other to a queen?
exercises.answer: A knight on b1 checks Ka3. A queen on b1 checks Ka2 after the bishop drives the king away from b1.

startContext: Begin immediately after the illustrated h8=Q at 57 seconds in the complete eleven-piece later diagram. The finite mate certificate covers both White king replies to a2+ and every subsequent defense, retaining Ne5 and White e3/e4/f4/g2. The source knight-promotion and king-return queen-promotion branches are shown; the omitted Kc1/b2 mate is explicitly independent. The earlier Kc3 move and alternatives to h8=Q remain unverified context, not a claim that the original position was lost or that promotion was White’s only move.
